scope: CBE pedestrian safety geometry and shared hull foundation; selected HBQ source comparison only, not whole-source parity.

selectedLines: 1810-1825: lateral free-space check includes nearby people
reference.disposition: HBQ separates people from generic obstacle rays and includes them in side-clearance observation. CBE keeps its existing friendly/on-foot braking extension and feature gates; this correction is CBE integration work, not an assertion that HBQ supplies the same braking model. Protected reference unchanged; no source code/assets imported.

finding: CortexInfantrySpeed projected people through vehicle model coordinates, then used model-unit/tilted gaps with world-metre braking constants. Scale changed distances and pitch/roll changed the vertical-overlap axis. Vehicle traffic already used a world frame; pedestrians did not.
implementation: Extend the existing DrivingHullInterval with an optional third unit axis requiring a valid second axis. One/two-axis result shapes remain2/4 values; triple returns6. Same corner and three edge transforms, independent third-axis extrema,0.05m outward padding and invalid/nonnumeric/finite guards.

Project own vehicle and pedestrian hulls onto horizontal right/travel and world vertical relative to one world origin. Reversing changes the travel axis, retaining physical asymmetric front/rear extents. Velocity projects into the same horizontal metre frame.

Unknown speed/own projection or selected pedestrian projection returns zero. Existing32-person refusal,250m discovery limit, one native query, friendly/on-foot filtering, feature defaults and final caller movement authority remain. Reaction/deceleration policy and3m margin remain, with shared outward boundary padding. No new movement command or controller.
cost: One own hull projection and4 native transforms/person instead of8 forward/inverse transform pairs/person. Shared single/dual-axis callers retain4 native transforms and skip optional third-axis work. Additional fixed dot/finite math; no new discovery/ray/worker/timer/cache. Native query cost and whole-frame median/p95 remain unmeasured.

validation.fixtures: Existing pedestrian case now checks shared caller/axis/invalid geometry contracts,0.5/1/2 scale gap mismatch, asymmetric reverse extents, and independent8-corner pitched height separation. Existing affine hull oracle and one/two-axis caller regressions remain. Offline mathematical/source checks only.
validation.result: Full pipeline passed first attempt. Runtime unchanged after build; reference/index/handover metadata postdates packaging. Unsigned development snapshot with unrelated pre-existing dirt.

remaining: Actual slopes/overpasses/reverse braking, native collision geometry and supported object scaling still need engine evidence.
